images.title: Turn 10 coins upside down in 3 moves
images.purpose: Shows that a triangle of 10 coins turns upside down by moving only the three corner coins.
images.composition: A before and after comparison: the triangle on the left, the inverted triangle on the right, one grey arrow between them. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: Left panel: 10 equal plain circles in a triangle pointing up, rows of 1, 2, 3 and 4 from top to bottom. The top coin and the two end coins of the bottom row are reddish purple (#CC79A7); the other 7 coins are teal (#0072B2). Label 'before' under the panel. A grey (#6B7280) arrow points right. Right panel: the same 7 teal coins in the same places, and the 3 purple coins moved: two now sit at the two ends of the second row, making it a row of 4, and one sits below the bottom, making a row of 1, so the triangle points down with rows of 4, 3, 2 and 1. Label 'after' under the panel. Centred above both panels, the label '3 moves'. Exactly 10 coins in each panel, 3 of them purple.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Keep the middle block still and move only the corners.
images.description: Shows that a triangle of 10 coins turns upside down by moving only the three corner coins.
images.context: 3, 6, 10, 15 coins need 1, 2, 3, 5 moves: the number of coins divided by 3, rounded down.

image_decisions.why: The puzzle answer is spatial; showing which 3 coins move is the whole idea.
